task: Write an introductory panel of about 70–110 words for a fictional small exhibition. Help first-time visitors understand its nonchronological arrangement and the touching rule. Retain the useful general explanation of what grouping similar materials helps visitors notice; do not replace it with promotional praise.

facts.text: The exhibition has five stations organised by material rather than by date.
Visitors may explore the stations in any order.
The curatorial purpose of grouping like materials is to make differences in wear easier to notice.
Items marked with a hand symbol are replicas that visitors may touch.
Items without the hand symbol should not be touched.
The captions explain how the original tools were used.

forbidden_additions: Permission to touch every item or a claim that the touchable replicas are originals.
Invented object ages, makers, discoveries, or visitor-study results.
preserve: The explanatory connection between grouping materials and noticing wear.
The symbol-based distinction between touchable replicas and other objects.
Visitors' freedom to choose their route.
